title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
lede: TechCrunch surveys AI agents you reach by text message instead of a separate app, from general assistants such as Instinct and Poke to ones built for families, travel and work.

points: Most share one pitch: keep context, connect to email and calendars, and carry out tasks such as bookings, reminders and purchases.
Instinct, valued at $10 billion after a $1 billion round, gives each assistant its own email address so it can open accounts and contact businesses.
Poke was the first AI agent approved on Apple Messages for Business, and its parent company was later bought by Cognition.
Fambot, Ohai and Orbits pull school, meal and chore schedules into one household plan; Miso focuses on travel.
Comma is free, open source and reachable over Signal, Telegram and WeChat; Folk runs tasks on its own private cloud computer.

sections.text: Messaging is becoming a front end for agents, and the products mostly differ in integrations, memory and how much they do without asking. Maverick asks permission first, while Instinct's own email accounts have raised privacy and security concerns.
